data.title: India’s Yes Bank reports quarterly profit but warns of hit from AT-1 judgment
data.description:
Yes Bank on Saturday reported a 65% jump in second-quarter profit to 10.80 billion rupees ($114 million), but said the figure did not reflect the impact of a Supreme Court ruling this week that set aside its 2020 write-off of 84 billion rupees ($884 million) of additional tier-1 bonds.

Had the impact been recognised, the bank would have posted a quarterly loss of 52.17 billion rupees after tax, it said in a filing.

($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

data.title: Hungary PM Magyar to present 2027 budget in parliament on Monday
data.description:
Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar will present the 2027 budget in parliament on Monday, targeting savings in public operating expenditure and planning for a surge in European Union-funded investments, he said on Saturday.

The 2027 budget is seen as a key credibility test for Magyar as he tried to curb the deficit to below the EU's 3% target ceiling while still honouring the pledges that helped secure his landslide election win over Viktor Orban in April.

Deutsche Bank said overseas investors had poured $13.5 billion into the local bond market year-to-date as of late September, betting heavily on centre-right Magyar's pledge to meet euro entry conditions by 2030.

"The TISZA government will spend more resources on those who have lost out in recent years, as well as on families, Hungarian businesses, pensioners, education and healthcare," Magyar said in a Facebook post.

"The 2027 budget will save money on the operation of the state and redirect funds from billionaires and polluting companies to the millions who have so far been left behind."

Magyar said billions of euros worth of European Union funding released after the rollback of Orban-era reforms seen as harming democracy would be used to launch "unprecedented" investments in housing, transport and water management.

Magyar's euro pledge has triggered a rally in Hungary's forint , which helped drive inflation sharply below the central bank's target. Market expectations for cuts in the deficit have bolstered government bonds.

Economists polled by Reuters see the deficit falling to 5.3% of output in 2027, compared with the government's 7.5% target for 2026. Analysts see Hungary joining the euro in 2032 or 2033.

data.title: Bank of Canada sees sharply higher inflation outlook as oil surges, Macklem says
data.description:
By Promit Mukherjee

The Bank of Canada expects to raise its quarterly inflation forecast significantly this month owing to persistently high crude oil and petroleum product prices, Governor Tiff Macklem said on Saturday.

New quarterly inflation and growth forecasts will feed into the BoC's rate decision on October 28.

"With the (Middle East) conflict ongoing, shipments still curtailed and refinery capacity damage, the risk that inflation broadens and becomes more persistent has gone up," Macklem told journalists on a conference call from Bangkok.

"Our beacon is our 2% inflation target, and we are committed to keeping inflation close to target over time. We are prepared to adjust monetary policy as needed."

Money market expectations of an increase in rates have been growing in the last few months but, as of Saturday, markets were not pricing in any change on October 28 or at the bank's last monetary policy decision of the year in December.

However, they are pricing in increases of 100 basis points over the course of next year. (0#CADIRPR)

Macklem said the global economy had shown resilience despite the conflict in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war, but that resilience was being tested by higher costs and tighter financial conditions.

He said governments also had less fiscal room to maneuver and needed to adjust their policies to rebuild that capacity.

For central bankers, the main concern is to ascertain whether higher oil and product prices will spill over into the broader economy.

Speaking about the decision to be made on October 28, Macklem said: "The question we are going to be asking ourselves is, 'Is inflation likely to come back down towards our target on its own, or are we going to have to raise interest rates to influence the path, nudge the path for inflation back towards the target?'."

data.title: Reliance Jio IPO GMP today: Listing-day jackpot or long-term bet? How should investors play Mukesh Ambani's mega IPO?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- The countdown to India's largest initial public offering (IPO) has begun. Jio Platforms IPO, backed by billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries Limited, is garnering heightened investors' interest ahead of the opening of its subscription period. Jio IPO's latest grey market premium (GMP) hints at 19.75% listing gains.

Jio Platforms is offering 27 crore new equity shares in the price band of between Rs.1,065 and Rs.1,119 per share to investors. Which makes the Jio IPO a Rs.30,213 crore issuance at the upper end of the price band. As all eyes are now on India's biggest ever IPO, let's understand whether the Jio IPO will be more than a listing day jackpot and long-term bet for investors.

Jio Platforms latest IPO GMP was recorded at Rs.221 at 2:02 pm on Saturday, October 17, as per media reports. With an upper price band of Rs.1,119 per share, the estimated listing price for the Jio Platforms IPO is Rs.1,340 (which is the sum of the upper price band and latest IPO GMP today). Considering the grey market premium of Jio Platforms IPO, the issue is likely to see 19.75% listing gain.

Investors must note that the grey market premium indicates demand for an issue in the unregulated market and is not an accurate representation of an IPO's listing day performance.

The IPO is a book-build issue of Rs.30,213 crores and an entirely fresh issue of 27 crore shares of Rs.30,213 crore. The IPO has fixed issue price band at Rs.1,065 to Rs.1,119 per share. The lot size for an application is 12 shares. The minimum amount a retail investor can put in Jio IPO is Rs.13,428 for 12 shares.

The IPO will open for subscriptions on October 21, 2026. The issue will close for subscription on October 23, 2026. The IPO allotment will likely be finalised for the Jio IPO on October 26, 2026. The IPO is expected to list on NSE and BSE on October 28, 2026.

Jio Platforms is well positioned to capitalise on India's growing digital economy, which is supported by its customer base of 533.3 million, extensive pan-India connectivity and approximately 60% share of wireless data traffic.

Jio IPO's valuation looks relatively attractive compared to Bharti Airtel's price to earnings ratio (P/E), according to Kantilal Chhaganlal brokerage, which goves 'Subscribe' rating for long-term perspective.

"At the Upper Price Band of Rs.1,119 and FY2026 P/E of 33.3x, the valuation appears relatively attractive compared with Bharti Airtel's stated P/E of 40.71x, while regulatory changes, competitive pressures and high capital expenditure remain key risks, Jio's market leadership, profitability and structural growth opportunities support giving Long Term Positive outlook . Hence, We Recommend Investor to Subscribe issue from Long Term Prospective," noted the brokerage in its report.

Jio Platforms Limited is a leading technology platform combining panIndia digital connectivity with digital services to drive India's digital transformation.

Its subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited has a 533.3 million customer base, as of June 30, 2026. Jio is not just a dominant player in the telecom industry but also continues to strengthen its technological capabilities.

data.title: Hurricane Trudy threatens western Mexico with heavy rain, coastal flooding
data.description:
Hurricane Trudy maintained its strength as it moved toward Mexico's western coast on Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen further before beginning to weaken on Sunday.

The US National Hurricane Center said Trudy was about 190 miles (305 km) south-southeast of Manzanillo early on Saturday, with maximum sustained winds of 90 mph (150 kph).

The hurricane was moving at about 8 mph (13 kph) and was forecast to approach southwestern and west-central Mexico later on Saturday before passing near the coast overnight into Sunday.

Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area on Saturday night, while tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across the region during the day, the NHC said. Hurricane conditions are also possible in areas under a hurricane watch.

Trudy is forecast to bring four to eight inches (10 to 20 cm) of rain, with isolated totals of around 15 inches, across parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco through the weekend, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, especially in steep terrain, according to the NHC.

Outer rain bands could produce two to four inches of rain, with isolated totals of around six inches, in Guerrero and Nayarit, where localized flash flooding is possible, the center said.

The NHC also warned of possible coastal flooding from storm surge in areas exposed to onshore winds, accompanied by large and destructive waves.

Swells generated by Trudy were already affecting parts of Mexico's southwestern coast and are expected to spread northward toward the country's west-central coast through the weekend, creating life-threatening surf and rip current conditions, the NHC said.

data.title: HDFC Bank's Q2 profit growth limited to 4.7% as treasury gains plunge 67%
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 17 -- HDFC Bank reported a 4.7 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 19,510 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, as a sharp 67 per cent decline in treasury trading gains weighed on earnings despite stronger income from its core lending business.

According to the bank's earnings release filed with the stock exchanges on Saturday, treasury trading gains fell to Rs 780 crore from Rs 2,390 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The decline limited overall profit growth even as net interest income, the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased by 9.7 per cent.

Highlighting the impact, the bank stated, "PAT, excluding treasury trading gains, grew by approximately 12.6% over the quarter ended September 30, 2025."

Net interest income rose to Rs 34,620 crore from Rs 31,550 crore a year earlier, supported by continued expansion in lending.

The bank said, "Net interest margin was at 3.16% on total assets, and 3.32% based on interest earning assets."

Net revenue increased to Rs 48,450 crore from Rs 45,900 crore, while fee and commission income rose to Rs 9,690 crore from Rs 8,840 crore.

Operating expenses stood at Rs 18,970 crore, while provisions and contingencies were Rs 3,570 crore during the quarter.

Despite pressure on earnings, asset quality improved.

"Gross non-performing assets were at 1.11% of gross advances as on September 30, 2026," the bank said, compared with 1.17 per cent in the preceding quarter and 1.24 per cent a year earlier.

Net NPAs stood at 0.37 per cent.

Total deposits grew 18.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 33.27 lakh crore, while gross advances increased 16.3 per cent to Rs 32.20 lakh crore.

The results highlight stronger core banking operations and improving asset quality, even as lower treasury gains restricted overall profitability.

data.title: HDFC Bank sees margins turning upwards from next quarter, says Sashidhar Jagdishan
data.description:
HDFC Bank expects its margins to recover from next quarter as the interest rate trajectory turns upwards, outgoing managing director and chief executive officer Sashidhar Jagdishan said, offering a positive outlook after the lender reported its lowest-ever net interest margin in the September quarter.

Jagdishan told CNBC-TV18 that margins had come under pressure during the quarter but expected the trend to change as the interest rate trajectory turned upwards. With a large part of the bank’s loan book linked to external benchmarks, he expects net interest margins (NIMs) to move higher.

The comments come as pressure on margins remains a key concern for investors, even as the bank reported healthy growth in its core lending business. HDFC Bank’s NIM declined to 3.16% in the September quarter, compared with 3.26% in the June quarter.

During the earnings call, Jagdishan said the bank’s topline growth had been healthy and expressed confidence in the resilience of its asset quality, which he expects to remain strong.

HDFC Bank reported a net profit of ₹19,510 crore for the September quarter, up 4.7% year-on-year and in line with estimates. Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 9.7% year-on-year to ₹34,620 crore. Deposits grew 18.8%, while the gross non-performing asset ratio stood at 1.11%.

The bank’s treasury trading income, however, fell 67.4% year-on-year to ₹780 crore, compared with ₹2,390 crore in the year-ago quarter. Excluding treasury trading gains, net profit grew 12.6% year-on-year, against reported growth of 4.7%.

Jagdishan backs continuity as Anup Bagchi prepares to take charge

With Anup Bagchi set to take over as managing director and chief executive officer after Jagdishan’s term ends on October 26, the outgoing chief highlighted the depth of the bank’s leadership and the importance of institutional continuity.

Speaking to CNBC-TV18, Jagdishan said HDFC Bank was not dependent on any one individual, noting that experienced leaders, including Kaizad Bharucha and Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, had played important roles. He expressed confidence that the depth of the management team would help preserve the institution’s continuity and ethos.

Jagdishan described Bagchi as a seasoned financial services professional with 34 years of experience across banking and insurance. He said the incoming chief was well placed to lead a team of capable leaders and wished him well ahead of the transition.

Bagchi, in his comments to CNBC-TV18, highlighted the strength of the institution and its team, saying the organisation remained committed to the bank. He added that much of the clean-up work was behind the lender, although some more work remained.

data.title: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund cash falls to 9.77% after Rajeev Thakkar's 'single-digit' outlook: Where is the money going?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, the country's largest active mutual fund scheme by AUM, has stepped up its investment deployment, reducing its allocation to cash and related instruments over the past six months.

The fund's factsheets show that its combined allocation to cash, debt and money market instruments, and arbitrage positions fell to 9.77% in September 2026 from 18.94% in March, nearly halving over six months. The share also dropped by 1.81 percentage points from 11.58% in August 2026. Here's what investors need to know.

Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund's September 2026 factsheet reiterates its focus on identifying individual investment opportunities rather than making allocation decisions primarily on the basis of macroeconomic conditions.

"We continue to look at individual investments on their own merits and will not hesitate to invest if an opportunity looks attractive," the factsheet stated.

It added that the fund had about 9.77% in cash holdings, debt and money market instruments, and arbitrage positions that could be deployed into long-term investments at appropriate levels.

The March 2026 factsheet had reported the corresponding allocation at 18.94%, while the August factsheet put it at 11.58%. The successive declines indicate that the fund has been reducing its deployable reserves as investment opportunities emerge.

In his August 2026 communication to unitholders, Rajeev Thakkar, CIO - Equity and Director at PPFAS, said the fund was increasingly finding opportunities to invest.

"Cash levels peaked at about 25%. They are down to about 14%-15% in Flexi Cap. We are increasingly finding opportunities to buy, and one may look forward to single-digit cash levels in some time," Thakkar said.

He also said that holding cash during the preceding two years had not harmed investor returns and had helped at the margin during a sideways market.

The September allocation of 9.77% seems to be consistent with the direction indicated in his August remarks.

According to the September 2026 factsheet, Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund (Direct plan) has delivered a 17.76% return since its inception on 24 May 2013, outperforming the Nifty 500 TRI benchmark's 13.56% return.

Over three years, the fund returned 12.21%, against 9.50% for the benchmark. Its five-year return stood at 11.15%, compared with 9.04% for the index.

However, the fund underperformed over the 1-year period ended 30 September 2026, declining 3.54% against the benchmark's 2.03% fall.

The fund completely exited Great Eastern Shipping Company in September 2026 and did not add any new stock to its portfolio.

It increased its holdings in 13 existing positions. DLF saw the largest addition by quantity, with the fund adding 390.64 lakh shares. Its holding rose from 137.10 lakh shares in August to 527.73 lakh shares in September.

Petronet LNG, Indus Towers and Indraprastha Gas were among the other stocks in which the fund increased its holdings.

The fund did not reduce the quantity held in any stock during the month. Its holdings in major companies, including HDFC Bank, Power Grid, ITC, Coal India, ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Infosys, remained unchanged.

The declining cash allocation and additions to existing positions suggest that the fund is deploying capital selectively rather than making broad changes across its portfolio.

data.title: Delhi Court Rejects Bail Plea Of Former Reliance Capital CFO Amit Bapna
data.description:
The court cited evidence of Bapna’s alleged role in corporate loan disbursements by RCFL and the bypassing of board sanctions at RHFL

A Delhi court has rejected the bail plea of Amit Bapna, former Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Reliance Capital, in an alleged bank loan fraud-linked money laundering case. The court cited evidence indicating his alleged role in loan disbursements by Reliance Commercial Finance (RCFL) and the bypassing of sanctions imposed by the board of Reliance Home Finance (RHFL).

Special Judge Vishal Pahuja, in an order passed on Thursday, said the evidence gathered by the prosecution indicated Bapna’s alleged control over the affairs of RHFL and RCFL.

“The evidence gathered by the prosecution agency against the applicant/accused (Bapna) is overwhelming and indicates towards his overarching control over the affairs of RHFL and RCFL,” the court said.

The court said the evidence indicated that Bapna was aware of transactions carried out by the companies and allegedly intended to benefit companies belonging to the Reliance Anil Ambani Group.

According to the court, large sums were transferred under the guise of general corporate loans without adequate verification of the borrowers’ financial positions.

The court also referred to evidence suggesting that shell entities with negative net worth were incorporated and used as conduits to siphon off public money.

The prosecution complaint, or chargesheet, and accompanying documents further indicated that Bapna allegedly exercised decision-making powers in RCFL without authorisation and proceeded with corporate loan disbursements despite sanctions imposed by RHFL’s board of directors.

Court Rejects Parity Argument

The court rejected Bapna’s counsel’s argument that the Enforcement Directorate (ED) had not arrested other co-accused who were allegedly similarly placed.

It observed that Bapna held a higher position in the functioning of Reliance Capital, RHFL and RCFL than the other accused. According to the court, he was at the helm of affairs, issued instructions to other co-accused and had some of them reporting to him.

The court also rejected the argument that Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, another co-accused, was the principal decision-maker and architect of the alleged offence under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), while Bapna had merely followed his instructions.

It said that even if Jhunjhunwala was considered the principal architect of the transactions, Bapna, in his capacity as CFO, was allegedly equally and proactively involved.

Custody & Bail Considerations

The court said Bapna was not entitled to bail solely because he had spent more than five months in custody. It noted that the investigation was continuing and cited the alleged scale of the offence, Bapna’s position and the possibility of influencing witnesses or tampering with evidence.

The court also distinguished Bapna’s case from that of Jhunjhunwala, who had been granted bail by the Delhi High Court. Referring to the prosecution agency’s chargesheet, it noted that Jhunjhunwala had received bail on medical grounds rather than on the merits of the case.

Dismissing Bapna’s plea, the court concluded that the grounds cited by the defence did not justify granting him bail at this stage.

data.title: Former IAS Officer SCL Das Appointed FSIB Head For 3 Years
data.description:
The government appoints former IAS officer Subhas Chandra Lal Das to lead the Financial Services Institutions Bureau, alongside six part-time members representing banking, financial institutions and insurance

The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet has appointed retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Subhas Chandra Lal Das as part-time chairperson of the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) for a three-year term, strengthening the body responsible for recommending senior appointments across state-run financial institutions.

The appointment will take effect from the date of notification or until further orders, whichever is earlier. The government has also appointed six part-time members to the bureau. The appointments cover public sector banks, financial institutions and insurance companies, bringing together former banking executives, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officials and insurance-sector leaders.

Six Members Appointed

The members representing public sector banks and financial institutions are Arijit Basu, former managing director of State Bank of India; Satish Kashinath Marathe, former director on the RBI Central Board; and Ramanathan Subramanian, former RBI executive director.

For public sector insurers, the government has appointed Siddhartha Mohanty, former chairman and managing director of Life Insurance Corporation of India; Neerja Kapur, former chairperson and managing director of New India Assurance Company; and T. L. Alamelu, former member of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI). All appointments carry a three-year tenure from the date of notification or until further orders.

Role Of FSIB

The FSIB recommends candidates for senior leadership positions in public sector banks, insurance companies and financial institutions, including NABARD, SIDBI, EXIM Bank and the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID). The bureau plays a key role in the government’s selection process for top management positions across state-owned financial institutions. The reconstitution brings banking, regulatory and insurance experience into the body overseeing recommendations for these leadership appointments.

data.title: Ujjivan SFB Profit Outlook Brightens As Loans Grow 32%, Secured Lending Expands
data.description:
Brokerage Elara Securities retains its Buy rating with an Rs 87 target price, implying 38% upside, as improving asset quality and lower credit costs support earnings prospects

Ujjivan Small Finance Bank reported a sharp rise in second-quarter FY27 profit, supported by strong revenue momentum, loan growth and lower credit costs, according to an Elara Securities report dated 17 October 2026. The brokerage retained its Buy rating on the stock with a target price of Rs 87, implying 38 per cent upside from its closing price of Rs 63 on 16 October. Net interest margin (NIM) declined by around 10 basis points sequentially to 8.4 per cent, reflecting a shift towards secured lending.

Elara expects the margin to ease further to about 8.3 per cent in the second half of FY27. The cost of funds stood at 6.9 per cent, but the brokerage flagged the possibility of a roughly 10-basis-point increase in the third quarter as the benefit from deposit repricing fades and higher repo-rate costs flow through. Loan growth remained strong at 32.4 per cent year-on-year, while deposits increased 29.2 per cent. The bank’s expanding secured portfolio and improving asset quality underpin Elara’s positive outlook, although deposit pricing and insurance commission regulations remain key risks.

Secured Lending Expands

Growth was broad-based across lending segments. Housing loans grew around 23.7 per cent year-on-year, micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) loans increased 43.5 per cent, and gold loans rose 209 per cent. Secured loans accounted for around 52 per cent of the portfolio, with the bank targeting a 56 per cent share by the end of FY27.

The bank added 66 branches during the quarter, taking its total network to 880. Operating expenses rose 11.8 per cent quarter-on-quarter and 26.1 per cent year-on-year, reflecting branch expansion and investment in its operating capacity. Management expects microfinance growth of 12–14 per cent for FY27. Elara noted that joint-liability group and individual lending each grew around 3 per cent sequentially.

Credit Costs Improve

Calculated credit costs declined by around 30 basis points sequentially to 0.95 per cent. Slippages stood at approximately Rs 180 crore, compared with Rs 170 crore in the previous quarter, while the slippage ratio remained around 1.6 per cent. Elara expects credit costs to remain near the bank’s full-year guidance of about 1 per cent, supported by better collections and lower provisions. The brokerage said the bank’s transition towards secured lending, alongside stabilisation in its microfinance and unsecured portfolio, could support a return on assets above 2 per cent in FY27.

It estimates return on assets of 2.3 per cent in FY27 and 2.2 per cent in FY28, with return on equity at 19 per cent and 18 per cent, respectively. Potential caps on insurance commissions proposed by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India could reduce FY28 return on assets by 10–20 basis points, Elara warned. Deposit pricing, the ability to raise the current account and savings account (CASA) ratio, and drought-related risks in Karnataka and Maharashtra also remain monitorable.

data.title: Axis Bank Q2 Profit Jumps 38% To Rs 7,003 Crore As NPAs Fall
data.description:
Strong loan and deposit growth, higher net interest income and improved asset quality support the lender’s quarterly performance, while margin pressures remain a key monitorable

Axis Bank reported a 38 per cent year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 7,003 crore for the second quarter of FY27, supported by higher net interest income, robust credit growth and an improvement in asset quality. The private sector lender’s net interest income (NII) rose 12 per cent year-on-year and 5 per cent sequentially to Rs 15,371 crore in the quarter ended 30 September 2026.

Core operating profit increased 11 per cent year-on-year to Rs 10,998 crore, while core operating revenue grew 10 per cent to Rs 21,817 crore. Fee income rose 6 per cent to Rs 6,381 crore, with granular fees accounting for 90 per cent of total fee income. Net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.36 per cent. Excluding the impact of foreign currency non-resident bank deposit (FCNR-B) mobilisation, the margin was 3.47 per cent. The cost-to-assets ratio declined to 2.14 per cent, down 24 basis points year-on-year, reflecting operating efficiency gains.

Advances And Deposits Grow

The bank’s net advances rose 23 per cent year-on-year to Rs 13.74 lakh crore, while total deposits increased 21 per cent to Rs 14.52 lakh crore. Retail advances grew 16 per cent, while small and medium enterprise (SME) loans increased 25 per cent. Corporate loans rose 34 per cent, reflecting sustained demand across business segments. Current account and savings account (CASA) deposits recorded year-on-year growth, with quarterly average balances increasing 14 per cent.

The month-end CASA ratio stood at 36 per cent. The bank reported raising Rs 1.018 lakh crore in FCNR-B deposits, supporting its deposit mobilisation strategy. Axis Bank continued to strengthen its digital banking and payments franchise. It held around 38 per cent market share in the Unified Payments Interface payer service provider segment and a 25.7 per cent share in merchant-acquiring terminals. Its mobile banking application had around 16 million monthly active users.

Asset Quality Improves

Asset quality strengthened during the quarter. Gross non-performing assets declined to 1.16 per cent as of 30 September 2026, compared with 1.46 per cent a year earlier. Net non-performing assets fell to 0.35 per cent from 0.44 per cent. The gross slippage ratio improved to 1.48 per cent, down 63 basis points year-on-year, while the net slippage ratio declined to 0.75 per cent. Net credit cost eased to 0.45 per cent, a reduction of 28 basis points from the year-ago period. The provision coverage ratio stood at 70 per cent.

The bank’s domestic subsidiaries also contributed to performance. Their combined profit after tax for the first half of FY27 rose 29 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,210 crore. Axis Finance reported a 42 per cent increase in first-half profit, while Axis Asset Management Company’s profit grew 36 per cent. For investors, the quarter reflects strong balance-sheet expansion and improving asset quality, alongside continued pressure to protect margins. Deposit costs, the sustainability of credit growth and the impact of funding mix changes will remain key factors shaping the bank’s earnings trajectory.

data.title: India Cements Q2 Results: Operational gains aid multi-fold profit growth, EBITDA jumps 78%
data.description:
India Cements, a subsidiary of UltraTech Cement, reported a sharp improvement in its September-quarter earnings, with net profit rising more than fourfold year on year as operational efficiencies and higher capacity utilisation strengthened its performance.

The cement maker reported a net profit of ₹38.8 crore for the quarter, compared with ₹8.8 crore in the corresponding period last year. Revenue from operations increased 2.2% year on year to ₹1,142 crore, from ₹1,117 crore in the year-ago quarter.

While revenue growth remained modest, the improvement in profitability was more pronounced. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 78% year on year to ₹145 crore, compared with ₹81 crore a year earlier. The EBITDA margin expanded to 12.7% from 7.3% in the corresponding quarter last year.

The company attributed the improvement in EBITDA and profit after tax (PAT) to operational efficiencies and an increase in capacity utilisation.

Capacity expansion and investment plans

Alongside the improvement in quarterly performance, India Cements is pursuing investments aimed at expanding its cement capacity and improving operational efficiency across its plants.

The company has approved investments of ₹2,000 crore, of which around ₹1,728 crore had been committed as of September 2026. Its ongoing plans include expanding cement capacity by 2.8 million tonnes per annum (MTPA), alongside investments in renewable energy and waste heat recovery systems.

The planned energy infrastructure includes 24 megawatts (MW) of waste heat recovery system (WHRS) capacity and 263 MW of renewable energy power. These initiatives are expected to support energy efficiency and help the company manage power costs, an important component of cement manufacturing expenses.

India Cements has also started upgradation projects across its plants. The work is expected to continue through the third and fourth quarters.

Shares of India Cements closed at ₹302.50 on the BSE on Friday, up 1.78%, ahead of the earnings announcement.

India Cements manufactures and sells cement and related products used in construction and infrastructure projects. It is a subsidiary of UltraTech Cement, part of the Aditya Birla Group.

data.title: Semiconductor ETF posts longest losing streak in over two decades amid chip selloff
data.description:
iShares Semiconductor ETF closed more than 4% lower on Friday, marking its ninth consecutive session of declines and capping its longest losing streak since May 2026 amid a broader selloff of chip stocks.

The fund, which tracks companies in the semiconductor sector, lost nearly 12% this week, its biggest weekly decline since April 2025, as all but two of the 34 constituents of the ETF ended in negative territory.

A selloff that began amid worries over the pace of AI buildout and credit concerns affecting CoreWeave deepened after the latest CPI report indicated a hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation, fueling fears over a more restrictive monetary policy from the Federal Reserve.

data.title: Binance bStocks Hits $1 Billion As Tokenized Stock Trading Accelerates
data.description:
TL;DR: Binance says its bStocks tokenized-equity offering has surpassed $1 billion in assets under management, four months after launch. The milestone illustrates growing interest in trading blockchain-based representations of traditional shares.

Binance says its bStocks platform has crossed $1 billion in assets under management, marking a significant milestone in its effort to make conventional financial assets tradable through cryptocurrency infrastructure.

The company reported the figure on October 15, approximately four months after the product launched. Binance also cited more than $40 billion in cumulative trading volume and an expanded range of tokenized US shares and exchange-traded funds.

The numbers suggest that traders are interested in moving between familiar Wall Street exposure and blockchain-based platforms.

What Tokenized Stocks Actually Offer

Eligible users can trade tokens designed to track exposure to underlying securities held through custody arrangements. Unlike holding ordinary shares directly, these instruments may not confer the same corporate voting or shareholder rights.

Their attraction lies in features such as fractional access, transferability and integration with other digital asset products.

Binance has already explored using tokenized equity holdings as collateral for derivatives positions, offering investors a reason to hold the instruments beyond simple price exposure.

That integration is one potential advantage over conventional brokerages, although it also introduces counterparty, custody and market-structure risks.

Regulatory Limits Remain

The products are not available to US persons and are subject to eligibility restrictions elsewhere. Tokenization does not remove the obligations surrounding securities trading.

For the broader sector, the important question is whether these products can continue attracting demand when crypto market enthusiasm weakens.

A $1 billion milestone is meaningful, but sustained growth will depend on transparent backing, dependable liquidity and the ability to offer advantages that conventional market infrastructure cannot easily reproduce.

data.title: Solana shows resilience, but some areas need continued observation, Fidelity says
data.description:
Solana has made significant progress in terms of network health across resilience, economic security and performance indicators, according to a Fidelity report.

Solana has had no reported mainnet outages in two years, but concentrations in stake, hosting and client software could threaten this, according to the report by Fidelity’s Center for Applied Technology (FCAT).

Related: Solana Foundation hires ex-Binance CMO and payments exec as new partnerships expand

Still, it noted that several areas surrounding decentralization and resilience warrant continued observation, including stake concentrates among a small number of validator identities and operators.

Coijntelegraph reported on Aug. 21 that Solana had reduced its slot time to 350 milliseconds, marking the first such reduction since the inception of the network, according to the Solana Foundation’s vice president of technology, Jacob Creech.

In June, the Solana Foundation shared plans to reduce slot times to 200ms, arguing that it would improve latency and accelerate confirmations on the blockchain network. Three further 50ms reductions are planned.

data.title: The Secret to Getting Colleagues to Say 'Yes' When You Ask for Something — WSJ
data.description:
By Vanessa Bohns

Most of us hate asking for things in the office. We don't want to impose. We anticipate rejection. It's just plain awkward.

That discomfort can lead us to ask for what we want in ineffective ways — or avoid asking altogether. We may bend over backward to make a meeting on time rather than simply asking to push it back 15 minutes, assume a deadline is firm without checking whether there's any flexibility, or offer vague complaints about needing extra help instead of actually requesting an additional team member.

It doesn't have to be like this.

Decades of research has found that people are far more willing to agree to our requests than we think — provided we know how to ask. And knowing how to ask isn't as complicated as we imagine. We just need to keep these few things in mind:

1. Ask directly

When you ask for something, make sure you actually ask for it.

Imagine your colleague says to you, "You know Steve, right? I'd really like to get connected with him."

How would you respond? You might say, "Steve's a really nice guy," or "You should go up to him at happy hour on Thursday." Both are friendly, supportive responses. However, neither answers the question your colleague thinks is being asked.

Now imagine instead the colleague says, "You know Steve, right? Would you be willing to connect me with him?"

Now there's no ambiguity. You know exactly what is being asked, and there is a yes or no answer to the question.

While this difference might seem obvious when we're on the receiving end of a request, it's much less obvious when we're the ones asking. In research I conducted with Francis Flynn, a professor at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, people asking for help tended to think that indirect requests would work just as well as direct ones.

In other words, we often think we're asking for something when really we're just hinting.

2. Ask in person

If possible, ask in person. If not, make a call. Don't ask by email.

In a study I conducted with Mahdi Roghanizad, an associate professor at the Ted Rogers School of Management, we found that people were 34 times more likely to say yes to a face-to-face request than to an emailed request.

While that study looked at requests made of strangers, in another set of studies we had participants make requests of people they knew. In one of those studies, participants asked five friends in person to help them with a brief proofreading task. Eighty percent of the people they asked agreed. In another study, participants made the same request by email, and only 29% agreed.

Email was also less effective than a phone call or video call. Both kinds of calls netted agreement from a little over 50% of both strangers and friends.

But again, this isn't something most people making requests are aware of. When we asked participants in these studies to predict how many people would agree to their requests, they expected the means of communication to make little difference.

When you combine our tendency to underestimate the value of asking in person with the convenience and comfort of firing off an email instead of walking down the hall or picking up the phone, it's easy to see why we can so often default to the least effective way of asking.

3. Assume a 'yes'

When you're asking for something, assume the other person is likely to say "yes."

My research over the past 20 years has consistently found that we underestimate the likelihood that people will agree to our requests. Participants in my colleagues' and my studies have asked more than 15,000 people for something — to lend a cellphone, donate to charity, locate a difficult-to-find building, count beans (literally). Before making these requests, we had participants guess how many people would agree. On average, we have found that people are about twice as likely to say "yes" to requests as our participants typically expect.

Keeping this in mind should give you more confidence to ask. But just as important, it should help you to strike the right tone when you do. If you're anticipating a yes, there's no need to be overly — and counterproductively — assertive. And because you're no longer expecting rejection, there's also no need to hedge, apologize or ask for less than what you really want.

4. Aim for more than 'yes'

When someone agrees because they feel compelled — not because they genuinely thought about and committed to their choice — they may end up regretting their decision, resenting the asker, or even backing out of the agreement later.

So, once you've made your best pitch, give the other person some time to think. You can do that after you've made your request, by telling the person to take a day to think about the answer. Or you can do it beforehand, by emailing someone a "heads up" about what you are planning to ask. Both are ways to show people you respect their autonomy, and trust that your requests have merit on their own.

A direct, in-person, self-assured request will help you get to "yes." Taking the extra step of honoring the other person's autonomy will help you get even more — a genuine, voluntary "yes."

Write to reports@wsj.com

data.title: A Divorced Couple's $10.7 Million Home Gave Their Family a Fresh Start — WSJ
data.description:
By Nancy Keates | Photography by Geloy Conception for WSJ

While living in Hong Kong, Los Angeles natives Jarlon Tsang and Julie Huang dreamed of giving their two children a California home that would provide a sense of permanence — a place they could come back to even after leaving for college. So they bought property in Palo Alto, Calif., and started building a new house.

They had been living in high-rise rental apartments in Hong Kong, where Tsang worked in venture capital focusing on the greater China region. For their new California home, they wanted openness and a big outdoor dining area — akin to how they had grown up. "We'd put 'home' on pause in Hong Kong," said Huang. "This was something I'd waited for."

Then, a few years into the $10.7 million project, Huang and Tsang divorced. Instead of abandoning or selling the property, they pressed on together, keeping ownership in both their names. They decided Huang would live in the six-bedroom home with their kids, who are now 17 and 20. Tsang, who still works in Hong Kong, comes to stay a few weeks at a time and during holidays, sleeping in the guest bedroom in the basement for maximum privacy.

When he's in town, they jointly hold all-day barbecues with their friends and family.

"This is his home too. I wanted it to be home for everyone," said Huang, 55, a communications consultant and former executive at Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba.

Tsang, 57, said the house allows them to have a place to be together. "They are still my family," he said. "We will always be a family."

The property is about 2 miles from Stanford University in the quiet, tree-filled neighborhood of Old Palo Alto, where Steve Jobs lived in an English Tudor before he died, and where Google co-founder Larry Page has a house.

Huang and Tsang paid $2.46 million for a 1940s-era cottage in the neighborhood in 2011. They were still living in Hong Kong at the time, but intended to move back to California. They rented the roughly 1,900-square-foot house out for several years before tearing it down and starting construction on the new home.

The build took almost five years, in part due to COVID delays, finishing in 2024. A key goal was getting as much natural light into the house as possible, said Christopher Roach of San Francisco-based architecture firm Studio VARA. That meant a modern design, with walls of windows and lots of skylights. To let in light, there is a screen wall between the dining room and front entry, with a massive piece of white marble on one side and slatted marble on the other.

Since they couldn't increase the square footage of the house, they aimed to maximize outdoor living space on the 8,000-square-foot lot. That led to the creation of a large inner courtyard, which has a kitchen and serves as an outdoor living and dining room. On the side of the house, a light court allows light into the basement, which has high ceilings to avoid a cavelike feel.

Huang's morning ritual is to open the shades in the main bedroom and let the sun pour in; she then walks down the stairway which is lit by a skylight at the top. Downstairs, she opens the sliding glass wall to the sun-lit courtyard. "It's peaceful. I feel the gift of light," she said.

Roach said he noticed little difference working with Huang and Tsang before and after they divorced. Maura Fernández Abernethy, a principal at Studio VARA, said they each took on different aspects of the project, with Huang focusing on the interior and Tsang on the landscaping and structure of the building.

The couple's son Dashel, 17, a senior in high school, said the new house was one way his family rebuilt their lives after the divorce. "When we moved in it felt like a fresh start," he said. He likes inviting friends over to use the large outdoor space and the basement, where he plays videogames, works out and watches movies. "The house helped me to be more open," he said.

Maddie, 20, is a junior at Duke University. When her father is at the house, she said, it's "very much like a normal dynamic," except that everyone has their own spaces. "The house was part of the separation, but it's also what brings us together," she said.

Huang said she's grateful they were able to keep the house as a happy place for the family, even if it's an unconventional arrangement.

"Nobody had to make a choice," she said. "It's been a big part of our healing."

data.title: IDBI Bank Profit Rises 4%; Operating Profit Jumps 33%
data.description:
Operating profit rises 33 per cent sequentially to Rs 2,893 crore as net interest income grows 29 per cent year-on-year and asset quality improves

IDBI Bank reported a net profit of Rs 2,205 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, marking a 4 per cent increase from Rs 2,115 crore in the June quarter. The lender’s operating profit rose 33 per cent sequentially to Rs 2,893 crore, supported by higher net interest income and improved operating performance, according to its Q2 FY27 results announced on 17 October 2026.

Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, increased 29 per cent year-on-year and 21 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 4,228 crore. Net interest margin (NIM) improved to 4.11 per cent, up 40 basis points year-on-year and 50 basis points sequentially.

Business Growth

The bank’s total business increased 18 per cent year-on-year to Rs 6.27 lakh crore as of 30 September 2026. Total deposits grew 17 per cent to Rs 3.56 lakh crore, while net advances rose 18 per cent to Rs 2.72 lakh crore. Current account and savings account (CASA) deposits increased 12 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1.56 lakh crore. The CASA ratio stood at 43.82 per cent at the end of September, reflecting the share of low-cost deposits in the bank’s overall deposit base. The cost-to-income ratio improved to 48.17 per cent, declining 385 basis points sequentially.

Asset Quality Improves

IDBI Bank’s gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declined to 2.12 per cent as of 30 September 2026, compared with 2.65 per cent a year earlier. The net NPA ratio improved to 0.17 per cent from 0.21 per cent in the corresponding period last year. The provision coverage ratio stood at 99.24 per cent, while the capital adequacy ratio improved to 27.10 per cent from 25.39 per cent a year earlier.

Tier 1 capital adequacy stood at 26.55 per cent. The results come days after the Union Cabinet approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,878 crore. The transaction is expected to be completed by March 2027, subject to the necessary processes and approvals.

data.title: ICICI Bank Q2 Profit Rises 20.1% To Rs 14,843 Cr As Loans Grow 30%
data.description:
Net interest income increases 17.7% to Rs 25,339 crore, while deposits climb 27.1% to Rs 20.50 lakh crore; net NPA ratio improves to 0.30% in the September quarter

ICICI Bank reported a 20.1 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 14,843 crore in the second quarter of FY27, supported by higher interest income, robust loan growth and an increase in fee income. The private sector lender’s net interest income (NII) grew 17.7 per cent to Rs 25,339 crore in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, from Rs 21,529 crore a year earlier.

Core operating profit rose 21.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 20,805 crore, while profit before tax, excluding treasury income, increased 23.4 per cent to Rs 19,954 crore. The results were approved by the bank’s board on October 17, 2026. The bank’s consolidated net profit increased to Rs 16,333 crore from Rs 13,357 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Loan Growth Remains Strong

ICICI Bank’s total advances grew 30 per cent year-on-year to Rs 18.32 lakh crore at the end of September 2026, compared with Rs 14.08 lakh crore a year earlier. Excluding loans extended by its international branches against FCNR (B) deposits, loan growth stood at 24.1 per cent.

The business banking portfolio expanded 33.8 per cent year-on-year, while the domestic corporate portfolio grew 30.6 per cent. The retail and rural loan portfolio increased 14.8 per cent and accounted for 51.6 per cent of the total loan portfolio at the end of the quarter.

Domestic advances grew 22.8 per cent year-on-year, while the overseas loan portfolio represented 7.8 per cent of the bank’s overall loan book.

The expansion in lending was accompanied by growth in deposits. Total period-end deposits rose 27.1 per cent year-on-year to Rs 20.50 lakh crore. Excluding FCNR (B) deposits, the increase was 17 per cent.

Average deposits grew 21.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 18.88 lakh crore during the quarter. Average current and savings account deposits increased 10.7 per cent, while the average CASA ratio stood at 35.8 per cent, reflecting an increase in the term deposit base following FCNR (B) deposit inflows.

Net Interest Margin Moderates

Despite growth in net interest income, the bank’s net interest margin (NIM) moderated to 4.18 per cent in Q2 FY27, compared with 4.36 per cent in the preceding quarter and 4.30 per cent in the year-ago period.

The bank said the benefit from interest on tax refunds was negligible in the September quarter, compared with eight basis points in the June quarter. Excluding this benefit, NIM in Q1 FY27 was 4.28 per cent.

Non-interest income, excluding treasury income, increased 12.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 8,277 crore. Fee income grew 20.1 per cent to Rs 7,795 crore, with retail, rural and business banking customers contributing around 75 per cent of total fees.

Operating expenses rose 8.5 per cent year-on-year to Rs 12,811 crore, slower than the growth in core operating profit.

The bank reported a treasury loss of Rs 230 crore in Q2 FY27, against a gain of Rs 220 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, primarily reflecting market movements. Consequently, standalone profit before tax increased 20.4 per cent year-on-year to Rs 19,724 crore.

Asset Quality Improves Further

ICICI Bank reported an improvement in asset quality, with both gross and net non-performing asset (NPA) ratios declining year-on-year and sequentially.

The gross NPA ratio fell to 1.20 per cent at September 30, 2026, from 1.58 per cent a year earlier and 1.38 per cent at the end of June 2026. The net NPA ratio declined to 0.30 per cent, compared with 0.39 per cent in September 2025 and 0.35 per cent in the preceding quarter.

Gross NPA additions stood at Rs 4,833 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 5,034 crore a year earlier. Recoveries and upgrades, excluding write-offs and sales, amounted to Rs 3,620 crore.

Provisions, excluding tax provisions, declined to Rs 851 crore from Rs 914 crore in the year-ago quarter. The bank continued to hold contingency provisions of Rs 13,100 crore at the end of September 2026, alongside an additional standard asset provision of Rs 1,283 crore relating to its agricultural priority sector portfolio, as directed by the Reserve Bank of India.

The provisioning coverage ratio on non-performing loans stood at 75 per cent.

Capital Position Remains Strong

The bank’s total capital adequacy ratio stood at 16.68 per cent at the end of September 2026, while its Common Equity Tier 1 (CET-1) ratio was 16.01 per cent. Both were above the respective regulatory minimum requirements of 11.70 per cent and 8.20 per cent.

During the quarter, ICICI Bank also acquired an additional 2 per cent stake in ICICI Life Insurance for Rs 1,470 crore.

Subsidiaries Report Higher Profits

ICICI Bank’s key subsidiaries also reported growth in profitability during the quarter.

ICICI Life Insurance’s profit after tax increased to Rs 374 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 299 crore a year earlier. Its value of new business rose to Rs 1,283 crore in the first half of FY27 from Rs 1,049 crore in the corresponding period last year, while its value of new business margin improved to 26 per cent.

ICICI Lombard General Insurance reported a 15.4 per cent increase in profit after tax to Rs 946 crore from Rs 820 crore. However, its combined ratio rose to 107 per cent from 105.1 per cent a year earlier, reflecting higher claims and expenses relative to premiums.

ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company reported a profit after tax of Rs 889 crore, compared with Rs 838 crore in the year-ago quarter. ICICI Securities’ consolidated profit after tax increased to Rs 439 crore from Rs 425 crore, while ICICI Home Finance reported a rise to Rs 220 crore from Rs 203 crore.

ICICI Bank’s consolidated assets grew 22.6 per cent year-on-year to Rs 32.93 lakh crore at September 30, 2026, reflecting expansion across its banking and financial services businesses.

data.title: Canada Eyes Fertiliser Exports To India As Fairfax Signals Fresh Investment
data.description:
Canada sees opportunities to expand fertiliser and potash supplies to India following Fairfax's plan to invest, and both countries target a trade pact by the end of 2026

India’s agriculture sector could benefit from Canadian fertiliser and potash supplies, while Fairfax Financial Holdings is looking to expand its investments in the country, Canadian Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu said. The remarks come as India and Canada work towards concluding a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement by the end of 2026.

Sidhu identified fertiliser and potash supplies as potential areas of cooperation, citing their possible role in supporting agricultural productivity in India as per a media report.

Fairfax Signals Further Investment

Sidhu highlighted Fairfax's proposed acquisition of a 60.7 per cent stake in IDBI Bank, which India approved on Tuesday. He described the Fairfax-IDBI transaction as the largest deal between the two countries in the financial sector and said it sent a signal that Canada was ready to deepen supply-chain engagement with India.

Trade Pact Talks Continue

The comments came as Indian and Canadian entities signed several commercial agreements and memoranda of understanding on Friday. Both countries reaffirmed their commitment to conclude negotiations on the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by the end of 2026.

The fifth round of CEPA negotiations took place in Ottawa from 5 to 9 October. Discussions covered market access for goods and services, investment, rules of origin, intellectual property rights and trade remedies. The next round is scheduled to take place in New Delhi in early November.

The proposed agreement aims to reduce trade barriers and improve market access for businesses in both countries. Government estimates suggest it could increase bilateral trade by USD 4.4 billion to USD 6.5 billion and raise Canada's gross domestic product by USD 3.8 billion to USD 5.9 billion by 2035.

Bilateral Trade And Investment

India-Canada bilateral trade stood at USD 7.96 billion in FY26, according to government data. India's exports to Canada increased from USD 4.22 billion in FY25 to USD 4.67 billion in FY26. India exported 5,517 different commodities to Canada during FY26.

Two-way merchandise trade reached USD 10.9 billion in 2025, comprising USD 3.9 billion in Canadian exports and USD 7 billion in imports from India. Foreign direct investment equity inflows from Canada to India totalled Rs. 31,204.9 crore, or USD 4.34 billion, between April 2000 and March 2026, according to official data.

data.title: HDFC Bank Deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha To Exit On December 31
data.description:
Bharucha’s planned exit follows the appointment of Anup Bagchi as the bank’s next managing director and chief executive, marking another leadership change at the lender

HDFC Bank Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha has sought to step down from his position effective December 31, 2026, the bank said in an exchange filing on Saturday, October 17. The development comes weeks after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) approved Anup Bagchi to succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan as the lender’s managing director and chief executive officer.

The announcement follows reports on October 16 that Bharucha was considering early retirement and could communicate his decision to the bank’s board in the coming days. The bank’s subsequent disclosure confirmed his intention to leave the role at the end of December.

Leadership Transition

Bagchi, a veteran of the ICICI group and the chief executive of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, is scheduled to take charge as HDFC Bank’s MD and CEO on October 27. Jagdishan’s current tenure ends on October 26, after he informed the bank in August that he would not seek reappointment. Bharucha had also been considered an internal candidate for the top job. He joined HDFC Bank in October 1995 and has served the lender for more than three decades. He became deputy managing director in April 2023 and joined the bank’s board in 2014.

Long Banking Career

As deputy managing director, Bharucha has overseen corporate banking, business banking, investment banking, rural banking and several retail lending businesses. His responsibilities have included emerging corporates, healthcare finance, infrastructure-related lending and inclusive banking initiatives.

His departure would mark a significant change in the bank’s senior leadership as it prepares for Bagchi’s tenure. HDFC Bank has not disclosed a successor to Bharucha in the available announcements. The transition comes as the lender works to sustain loan growth, strengthen its deposit base and manage post-merger integration following its 2023 merger with HDFC.

data.title: Fancy a beer after a run? Make it a celebratory drink not recovery strategy
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- Scotland's middle-distance runner Josh Kerr broke the world record for the mile (1,600m) in London this July.

It happened when he participated at the annual, one-day international track and field competition, London Athletics Meet. Minutes after running the distance in 3 minutes 42.66 seconds to improve the record that had gone unchallenged since 1999, Kerr said he would celebrate with "a couple of pints." Cricketers from England and Australia are well known for their pub visits with former England captain Ben Stokes' one recent pub outing dragging on well beyond the midnight curfew leading to headline-making consequences.

When professional athletes, among the fittest and fastest humans in the world, unwind with a drink or two, there's simply no argument strong enough to suggest that libations and active life don't mix well (in moderation). In fact, as sport and exercise have emerged as social occasions in the post-pandemic years, there have been a lot of entrepreneurs, groups and gyms that conduct events with alcohol on the menu. I have been mixing the two for a while now knowing well that no amount of exercise can counter the ill effects of alcohol but like millions of others I do so for the social and fun aspects of it. Here's my pick of the best of both worlds.

The place is so stunningly beautiful and awe-inspiring that musician Sting, designer Giorgio Armani and actor Colin Firth have homes there. Imagine a whole week of yoga during the day in the open, lush green fields with a cool breeze under the Tuscan sun and unwinding with some curated Italian wine watching the sun set in a vineyard far from the maddening crowds?

Sounds like the best of all worlds. That's exactly what Natasha Mahindra curates with Anam Cara Retreats. Last year she held a successful yoga retreat with wine tastings and more in Italy's Tuscany region. This year she mixed yoga with sundowners in Greece, Spain and Spiti Valley in the Himalayas.

Mahindra is among a growing number of yoga teachers who are bringing yoga up to speed with the demands of the post-pandemic world: yoga still rooted in tradition but with a schedule that allows you to relax, make connections and have fun too. After all, one needs it all to cope with the stress and chaos of present day life.

Occasional drinking has little lasting impact, the body recovers between instances, says Ashwini V Rai, a fitness expert at Cult. "Regular or heavy drinking is the bigger issue, since it steadily undercuts sleep, stress resilience and clarity, no matter how consistent the yoga practice is. In short, it's not that the two can't coexist, but the more frequently and heavily someone drinks, the more it works against what yoga is meant to deliver," she explains.

A decade ago, I was so thirsty after running the Chicago Marathon that I drank two pints at the finish line, where free beer was being served to all finishers. Thankfully, Kerr and I are not the only people who enjoy a couple of pints after a race. Running and drinking have gone hand-in-hand for a long time. The eccentric, global, non-competitive social running club Bombay Hash House Harriers have been running to their pints since 1938.

Today, there is a much more organised group, Race Days and IPAs, that brings together runners who enjoy their pints. Ahead of its fifth anniversary, the invite-only group has finally opened up and anyone who enjoys both running and beer in any part of the world can sign up on their website racedaysandipas.com.

"The group was built on the simple idea: run hard, then celebrate harder. What began in November 2021 as four friends has grown into chapters in New York City, Westchester and India," says co-founder Greg Waters from New York City. "The club is a community of runners of all paces and abilities, united by a love of the sport and the post-run debrief. Whether you are chasing a personal record, or just chasing the beer, there's a place for you."

Each member's mileage and workouts are tracked through Strava and displayed on a leaderboard. It has an AI-powered coach that analyses your exercise data from Strava and suggests what areas and training sessions you ought to focus on. Members also post their pictures - as many of their runs as also pints that follow after. The New York City members meet for a post-work run in Central Park every Thursday and head for a communal pint at 7pm sharp. The India group, active mainly in Bengaluru, usually meet on Sunday mornings and head for dosas more often than beer.

Generally speaking, immediately after a prolonged or intense event such as long-distance running or Hyrox, the body is primarily trying to restore fluid balance, replenish glycogen and repair muscle tissue. Alcohol does not help with any of these processes, warns Dr Rinkesh Kumar Bansal, director for gastroenterology, Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Gurugram. "A celebratory drink is a social decision, but medically it should not be regarded as part of recovery. The larger the amount of alcohol consumed, the greater the potential for dehydration, sleep disruption, gastrointestinal symptoms and impaired recovery," he clarifies.

While warming up for my first Hyrox, I overheard two men on the spin bike saying, "All I need after the event is some beer." Like Crossfit before it, Hyrox participants do enjoy their drinks at the end of a rather tough sport they willingly participate in. Prashanth Ponnappa, personal trainer and co-founder of The Troop Fit in Bengaluru, has participated in Hyrox races in India and in Thailand.

"What's missing in the India Hyrox events is the fun elements. Bangkok Hyrox was a lot more fun with much more food and drinks options at the venue. There were stalls selling cold beer at the Bangkok Hyrox and that's been missing in all three Indian cities that have hosted Hyrox," says Ponnappa, who enjoys a cold one after a hot and sweaty race.

Rai says that after an event like Hyrox, the body is usually dehydrated and depleted of fuel, so your first priority is to rehydrate and eat a proper meal. "Drinking on an empty stomach tends to hit harder, and it can slow recovery. Once those basics are covered, a celebratory drink in moderation should be fine for healthy people," she suggests.

Both pickleball and padel are as much, or more, social outings as they are a sport. From the very beginning both these racquet sports have been used as mixers by dating apps, sports brands and alcohol brands as these two trending sports attract an audience all these businesses target. Unlike running, both pickleball and padel allow players to chat and interact with each other between games and share moments and jokes between points.

It is not uncommon for weekend padel games to lead people straight to boozy brunches and a relaxed bar to chat over easy drinks. There are plenty of events in urban India that combine padel, pickleball and cocktails on weekends. The online platform, District by Zomato, has listed such events multiple times. Tinder Padel was a popular mixer in cities like Mumbai and Bengaluru last year.

Whatever your reasons for drinking after playing a sport, it is clear that there is no physiological benefit of alcohol that is necessary for exercise or recovery, says Bansal, and adds, "The perceived advantages are generally social - celebration, relaxation and participation in a group ritual-rather than benefits to fitness or recovery. Recover first, celebrate second and remember that alcohol is a celebratory choice, not a recovery strategy."

data.title: Railway PSU stocks derailed! RVNL, IRFC, IRCON, RITES to IRCTC down 60% in yr- What went wrong? Experts explain
data.description:
Railway PSU stocks, Oct. 17 -- Top railway public sector undertaking stocks, including Rail Vikas Nigam Limited, Indian Railways Finance Corporation (IRFC), IRCON International, RITES, to Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC), have seen a sharp decline of up to 40% over the past year.

The steep correction has left investors wondering what went wrong and whether the worst is over. Let's understand from experts, along with their take on railway PSU stocks outlook.

The decline in railway PSU stocks is more of a correction after decades of rally, according to Tushar Badjate, Director of Badjate Stock & shares Pvt Ltd.

"This is a valuation correction first and an earnings correction second. In 2023 and 2024, these stocks were priced for a decade of perfection. IRCTC hit an all-time high of Rs.1,318 in May 2024 and is now down about 61% from that peak. RVNL and IRFC have fallen between 45% and 53% from their 52-week highs," added Badjate while highlighting that three things went wrong for these PSU stocks.

Slow growth and decline in margins were among the key things that went wrong for railway PSUs. "What did not break is spending. Railway capex for FY27 is a record Rs.2.93 lakh crore. The money is flowing. It is just not reaching these companies at the old margins," highlighted Badjate.

PSU stocks often attract heightened investor interest because of their government-backing, relative stability and long-term growth prospects. The sharp correction in railway PSU stocks is largely a result of investor expectations running ahead of fundamentals, according to Tushar Badjate.

However earnings concerns are real and they are about margins not orders, underlined the expert.

"Order books look healthy. RVNL has Rs.93,492 crore and RITES has a record Rs.9,445 crore. The problem is conversion. Only about Rs.40,000 crore of RVNL's book is actually under execution. Its EBITDA margin is just 4.4%. IRCTC grew revenue 18% last quarter, yet profit was flat as its margin fell to 28.2% from 34.3%. IRCON's consolidated profit dropped to Rs.92.7 crore from Rs.164.6 crore on losses from joint ventures. These companies are no longer protected monopolies. They are contractors competing for work. Contractors do not deserve 50 to 60 times earnings," he added.

The correction has improved valuations for some railway PSU stocks not for all of them in the segment, noted Badjate calling IRFC a safer choice for conservative, income-focused investors.

Over the next 12 months, Nitant Darekar, Research Analyst at Bonanza, expects railway PSUs to ride a sustained capex cycle with Indian Railways' FY27 capital outlay at a record Rs.2.93 lakh crore.

"RVNL offers the deepest visibility with a Rs. 93,492 crore order book, guidance of about 15% revenue growth and diversification into ports, hydro and overseas work, though thin margins cap upside," explained Nitant Darekar, Research Analyst at Bonanza.

IRFC stock's primary trend remains bearish as the ongoing momentum hints at series of lower highs and lower lows from its peak. "Although the RSI at 52.56 indicates a slight neutral recovery attempt, it lacks decisive momentum. This is not a fresh buying opportunity because the stock remains trapped under a heavy bearish structure," stated Virat Jagad, Sr. Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza.

Downtrend defined by continuous sliding from above 720 to its current level highlights IRCTC's outlook.

"All key moving averages are aligned in a downward bearish stack-20 EMA (463.97), 50 EMA (474.05), 100 EMA (494.56), and 200 EMA (539.51)-with price consolidating right around the 20 EMA," highlighted Jagad, while adding caution that it is not a fresh buying opportunity as buying into an ongoing, structurally weak downtrend carries high risk.

Akin to other peers in the category, RVNL also remains locked in a persistent downward trend. The stock is hovering close to its 20 EMA, while it remained firmly suppressed underneath its 50 EMA, 100 EMA and 200 EMA.

"An RSI reading of 47.05 reflects weak neutral momentum with no strong bullish divergence present on the daily chart. This is not a fresh buying opportunity because current price action merely represents a minor relief bounce within a broader drop," noted Virat Jagad.

RailTel is displaying a strong long-term bearish bias as it declines from above 380 to current levels around 255.40. "The RSI at 45.60 sits below the neutral 50 threshold, highlighting persistent underlying weakness. This is not a fresh buying opportunity due to heavy overhead supply across multiple moving average barriers," Jagad added.

New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- No outdoors getaway or party is complete without the right set of tracks setting the mood. Sure you can play songs on your smartphone, but that is often not enough especially when you are out with a group of friends or family members.

This is where a compact Bluetooth speaker becomes important. The right speaker that is somewhat light in weight, is easy to carry, last long enough between charges and sound good for its size is what you need to on road trips or at picnics. That said, buying the smallest or cheapest model does not always guarantee a satisfying listening experience. Some compact speakers prioritise portability over battery life, while others offer longer playback but take up more space in your bag.

Before choosing one, look at three essentials: battery backup, sound quality and portability. A longer-lasting battery means fewer charging breaks during travel, while clear vocals and balanced bass can make music and podcasts more enjoyable. Weight, water resistance and build quality also matter if you plan to use your speaker outdoors or carry it around regularly.

To help you find the right fit, we have compared five portable mini speakers across these key factors. This list explores what each model offers, from pocket-friendly designs to options built for longer listening sessions. Whether you are shopping on a tight budget or willing to spend more for better features, this guide will help you find the right model for your needs.

The JBL Go 4 is a compact Bluetooth speaker designed for music on the go, with a lightweight build that easily fits into a bag or pocket. Its IP67 rating provides protection against dust and water, which makes it suitable for outdoor adventures, poolside listening and travel. The rugged design adds everyday practicality, while Bluetooth connectivity enables wireless music playback from compatible devices. A USB Type-C port handles charging, and the built-in battery offers up to seven hours of playback.

Buyers find the speaker's sound quality amazing and appreciate its portability, being easy to carry outdoors and perfect for travel, with one customer noting it fits in the palm of their hand. They praise its compact size, appearance, and seamless Bluetooth connectivity, and consider it good value for money.

Buyers should choose this Bluetooth speaker for its sound quality, connectivity and design.

The Sony ULT Field 1 is a rugged portable Bluetooth speaker built for listeners who want punchy bass and dependable battery life. Its dedicated ULT button boosts low frequencies, giving music a deeper, more energetic sound, while Sony's Sound Diffusion Processor helps deliver a more expansive listening experience. The compact speaker features a detachable strap for easy carrying and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. Its battery promises up to 12 hours of playback.

Buyers praise the speaker's sound quality, describing it as ultra clear and balanced, while also appreciating its build quality and compact size. The battery life is impressive. They find it easy to carry and use, making it ideal for home and work outdoor use.

Buyers should choose this sound quality, battery life and connectivity.

The boAt Stone 1200 Pro is a portable Bluetooth speaker built for listeners who want powerful sound and bass-heavy music. Its 60W output, two 2.75-inch full-range drivers and dual radiators aim to deliver punchy bass and clear highs for parties and outdoor gatherings. The rugged, elongated design includes a carry strap for easier transport and an IPX6 rating for protection against water splashes. Battery life reaches up to 7.5 hours at 50% volume, while True Wireless Stereo pairing lets you connect two compatible speakers for a bigger soundstage.

Buyers find the speaker's sound quality amazing and appreciate its impressive battery backup, with one mentioning it can run for 6-7 hours on 50% charge. The build quality is excellent, and they consider it worth the price point.

Buyers should choose this sound quality and battery life.

The JBL Charge 6 combines a rugged, portable design with powerful JBL Pro Sound, delivering rich bass and crisp highs for music at home or outdoors. Its AI Sound Boost technology analyses audio in real time to improve output while reducing distortion. The removable handle strap makes carrying easier, while IP68 protection guards against dust and water. Battery life reaches up to 24 hours, with Playtime Boost adding four more hours.

Buyers find the speaker's sound quality excellent, particularly praising its crisp clear vocals and bass performance. They appreciate its appearance and consider it well worth the money.

Buyers should choose this sound quality and design.

The Xiaomi Sound Outdoor 30W features a compact, cylindrical design with an anti-slip lanyard, making it convenient for travel, picnics and outdoor gatherings. Its 30W audio system combines a 20W woofer, 10W tweeter and dual passive radiators for punchy bass and clear highs. The IP67-rated body resists dust and water, while Bluetooth 5.4 enables wireless streaming. Its 2,600mAh battery promises up to 12 hours of playback at 50% volume, and USB-C charging takes approximately 2.5 hours.

Buyers praise the speaker's sound quality, with one noting it fills a 200 square feet room at 40% volume, and its 12-hour battery life at 50% volume. Moreover, the build quality is excellent.

Buyers should choose this sound quality, battery life and design.
